widgets_values: @Image1 defines the woman: keep her face, the copper-red blunt bob with fringe, the freckles, the deep red lip, the oversized amber leather trench coat, the black turtleneck, the wide black trousers and the boots exactly as they are. @Image2 defines the bottle: a faceted amber glass flask with a brushed-brass atomizer cap; keep its shape, facet count, proportions and material exactly. @Image3 defines the first place: keep the brutalist board-marked concrete, the colossal arched window, the single hard shaft of light across the polished terrazzo and the travertine bench exactly as they are. @Image4 defines the second place: keep the board-marked concrete parapet, the stone tiled floor, the long low shadows and the hazy skyline under a low sun exactly as they are; add no furniture, no signage, no skyline towers that are not there. A four-shot fragrance commercial where each shot demonstrates one property of the product, hard cuts between shots, every shot moving in camera or in light, nobody walks toward the camera and nobody looks at the lens. SHOT 1, extreme macro, in the first place: the flask held between her fingers inside the light shaft, one press of the brass atomizer, a fine cold mist shooting through the beam and hanging in the air as glittering droplets; the camera pushes in on the nozzle and the glass, focus riding from the brass to the liquid inside. SHOT 2, cut to the second place at golden hour: the same fine mist drifting and spreading across the terrace in the low sun, carried further than it should be able to reach, lifting the hem of her coat and a strand of hair; she stands still at the parapet with her back to camera, only the wind moves her; the camera cranes up slowly behind her. SHOT 3, cut back to an extreme macro on the stone: the low sun passing through the amber glass throws a warm caustic onto the concrete, and as the sun drops the caustic stretches and slides, shifting from amber to rose; the glass glows from inside, the liquid catching the last direct light; the camera slides with the caustic. SHOT 4, cut to a low hero: the flask alone on the concrete parapet against the dusk sky, one last glint running along the facet, the light going out of the frame, dust still hanging; the camera tilts up slightly and holds. Cinematic high-fashion campaign, hard contrast between warm light and cold shadow, shallow depth of field in the macros. Sound: one crisp atomizer hiss, a low sub pulse under the cuts, wind on the terrace, glass ringing softly once at the end.

nodes.title: Note: Reference Roles
widgets_values:
**Input Assets**

- [kling4_r2v_woman_amber_trench.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_r2v_woman_amber_trench.png) — character reference colour / wardrobe / face
- [kling4_r2v_amber_flask.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_r2v_amber_flask.png) — product reference (shape, material, cap)
- [kling4_r2v_brutalist_atrium.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_r2v_brutalist_atrium.png) — first location (architecture, light shaft, materials)
- [kling4_r2v_brutalist_terrace.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_r2v_brutalist_terrace.png) — second location (parapet, low sun, skyline)

## One shot, one product property

The video node already carries the character, the object and the places; what makes the five seconds an ad instead of a moving still is that **each shot demonstrates one property of the product and nothing else**: the atomizer's spray as a cold mist shot through a light beam, the trail travelling across a second location, the low sun passing through the amber glass and throwing a caustic that shifts colour as the sun drops, and finally the object alone holding the last light. State the property the shot is proving, not only what happens in it.

Cut between the two locations instead of moving the camera between them: a cut reads as budget and intent, a pan reads as a camera operator with nowhere to go. Give every shot its own camera behaviour (push in on the nozzle, crane up behind her, slide with the caustic, tilt and hold) and let the light itself change inside the later shots — a sun that drops during the cut is what sells the time passing.

Never write "she walks toward the camera holding the bottle and looks at the lens". That is the shot every video model defaults to and it has no attitude and no product information.

## How references work

Each reference image is bound to a slot in socket order: the first image connected becomes `@Image1`, the second `@Image2`, and so on up to ten images; up to five reference videos become `@Video1…@Video5`. A reference does nothing on its own — the prompt has to hand it a job and forbid the model from changing it. Name the role, then list the invariants (`keep … exactly as they are`) for every attribute you care about, otherwise Kling blends all references into one averaged subject.

Give each reference a different job. Two people references fight over the same identity; a person, a product and a room in one prompt read as three separate instructions and stay distinct. Stating the invariants is what keeps the coat, the flacon's facet count and the arched window stable between frames.

## Filling in the extra reference slots

Only `image_1` exists when the node is first placed; `image_2 … image_10` appear as the previous slot gets connected. When driving the API directly, send `model.reference_images.image_1`, `model.reference_images.image_2`, … in the request body — adding the extra slots by hand in the frontend can drop `image_1` from the serialized prompt.

## Cutting it like a commercial

A single locked-off action reads as stock footage however good the light is. Write the prompt as a shot list instead: label each shot (`SHOT 1, macro` / `SHOT 2, wide` / `SHOT 3, medium tracking` / `SHOT 4, low product hero`), say `hard cuts` explicitly, and give every shot its own camera movement and its own light behaviour. Four shots inside five seconds is accepted; the cuts land where the prompt implies.

Give the product its own macro shot. In a reference-to-video prompt the character and the room are what the model wants to spend the shot on, so the product only becomes a hero object if it gets a dedicated close-up with the light doing something to it (a beam crossing the glass, a caustic thrown on the floor). End on the product, not on the person leaving.

Never ask for the model to walk toward the camera holding the product and look at the lens: that is the shot every model defaults to, and it has no attitude. She should be doing something to the object, or the object should be alone and she should be the event that crosses it.

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)
